The study infers that incentive stakes sit mostly in credit, since Regulation II bars net network compensation to debit issuers with 10 billion dollars or more in assets.
The study infers that a partner-facing comparison will often show a gap, given Discover's 28 million dollar deferred balance against billions at Visa and Mastercard.

decision.question: Should the issuer deal view show the incumbent incentives a large bank would put at risk beside the network's own economics?
options: Show the network's own economics only
Show partners net economics over the contract term beside a blank incumbent-incentive line the issuer fills in
Keep the incumbent-incentive line in the agent's deal flow for partner managers, and show partners the network's economics
decision.evidence_favours: The third option while the gap stands, with the second ready if the credit bill moves. Discover's deferred incentives were 28 million dollars against billions at Visa and Mastercard (dgn-382, visa-451, mastercard-415). The owner names signing bonuses and exclusive deals as limits on its business (dgn-383, dgn-384). The bill has sat in committee since January 2026 (cross-194). Pricing stays the business's lever, and the experience makes the trade visible.

position.text: Visa and Mastercard recorded 15.75 and 20.5 billion dollars of incentives in their 2025 years. Their capitalised balances were 7.3 and 10.4 billion dollars, against Discover's 28 million dollar deferred balance at end-2024. The accounting differs, so the comparison is indicative. American Express negotiates each issuer rate privately. For debit issuers with 10 billion dollars or more in assets, Regulation II limits net incentives whichever network pays them.

means.text: Build the large-issuer case on the whole relationship over the contract term, with incentives at risk as a line the issuer enters. Keep Visa and Mastercard names and figures off the page. Present the second-network rule as a bill in committee.

Clearway has no economics view, so an issuer deal module is new work. Its agent deal flow should carry a blank incumbent-incentive line, so a partner manager prices against the issuer's alternative. Totals cover the contract term with no break-even date, under the no-timings rule.

objection.text: A large bank could object that when Discover cannot match up-front payments, the comparison mainly shows the loss from switching and argues against the network.

resolution.text: The study has no source on how issuers would read such a view, so its effect on trust is an inference to test with issuers. Keeping the incumbent line in the agent's deal flow lets partner managers price against it without showing partners the gap. If passed, the credit bill would stop covered issuers limiting credit cards to Visa and Mastercard, and bar penalties for missing a set volume on one network. The bill has sat in committee since January 2026. Visa's filing says some clients can leave on relatively short notice without significant early termination fees.

cards.limit: Both incentive totals are global. Visa's contracts cover sellers and other partners as well as banks, and Mastercard says it also pays incentives to some larger merchants (visa-468, mastercard-423). Discover's 28 million dollars is a deferred balance under its own accounting policy, so the comparison is indicative (dgn-382). Individual deal and clawback terms are not public (mastercard-105). The portfolio-wide reversal is one analyst's view, given in the context of a possible sale of Fiserv's debit networks (visa-453).

cards.title: Reading is mostly open around closed network specifications, and the Visa, Mastercard, American Express and Discover developer centres each require an account before a sandbox key

observed.text: Mastercard lets signed-out readers open the documentation of all 94 services its llms.txt lists, though some catalogue products show an overview only.
Visa marks 20 of the 73 products in its API browser as restricted, and American Express holds the specifications of five of 18 listed products for invited readers.
Mastercard, American Express and Discover keep network specifications behind a sign-in, and Visa's rules class VisaNet information as confidential.

Discover's Partner Product Portal serves an OpenAPI specification for each of its twelve products to signed-out readers, while its Developer Center admits developers only by a representative's invitation.
Visa and Mastercard open a sandbox for most APIs to any registered developer before a commercial agreement, while American Express's dashboard asks developers to request keys for review.
Visa Acceptance's API console and Authorize.net's reference load default sandbox credentials for signed-out readers, and the study did not press Send.

inference.text: The study infers a reader's own key surfaces authentication problems early. Developers report Cybersource requests that work in a portal console and then fail with authorisation errors from their own client.
The study infers a public ISO 8583 mapping supports an early feasibility reading and cannot replace the network specification, which American Express requires for every host certification.

decision.question: Which single access policy should the developer site, Clearway and the story share for the reference, the sandbox key and the test cards?
options: Public reference and test cards, with a sandbox key from a self-serve preview account before a participation agreement, as decisions.md records
A sandbox key only with the NDA or after contracting closes, as Clearway shows today
A signed-out console on shared default credentials, as Visa Acceptance's console loads
Access by a representative's invitation, as Discover's Developer Center runs today
decision.evidence_favours: The first. It is parity with Visa and Mastercard's self-serve sandboxes and ahead of American Express's key review and Discover's invitation (visa-190, mastercard-002, amex-386, dgn-034). Visa limits capture, sale, refund, void and verification to pre-approved clients even in sandbox, so the business should scope what a preview key reaches (visa-432). Today the developer site, Clearway and the story brief each state a different policy.

position.text: Discover's twelve public OpenAPI specifications put it ahead of American Express's invitation-only specifications. It is level on gated network specifications. Its invitation-only Developer Center, whose documentation returns 403, is behind Visa and Mastercard's self-serve sandboxes.

means.text: Keep the sandbox behind the preview account, as decisions.md records, and take the shared demo credentials off the quickstart. Fix the lines that still call the sandbox public, on the home hero, in account.html's intro, in account.js's header comment and twice on the docs home. The support page says 'No agreement' beside 'By continuing you accept the API terms'. Carry that terms line into the sign-up dialog, as Visa Acceptance's sandbox sign-up embeds its terms. Drop the lines that time the partner's pace, such as 'in a minute', 'ten minutes', the Takes column and 'in an afternoon'. The docs home's '41 ms' and 'within a second' need Rich's ruling under the no-timings rule.

Clearway's onboarding screens and MSG-4481 hold the sandbox key until contracting closes, while its developer guide issues the key with the mutual NDA. Align both to the chosen policy. The same guide times the key at about two minutes and the quickstart at about twenty, and both lines should go under the no-timings rule.

The build's panel 1 has Priya press Try it out, create a preview account and get one authorisation approved before anyone signs. Script v3's panel 1 still puts documentation behind that sign-up, against decisions.md, and product-brief.md still has Marcus open the sandbox in panel 3. Update both, and delete the uncalled Open to you now list in js.txt, which says no key is issued. Keep the narration on what Priya holds before signing, her own key and an approved authorisation.

Building in a sandbox before a commercial agreement is parity with Visa and Mastercard, and a change from Discover's invitation today. A public ISO 8583 mapping is parity with Mastercard, whose developer file host serves a 64-page mapping of an authorisation response to ISO 8583:87 data elements with no login. The study found no public mapping at Visa, American Express or Discover. Decide deliberately what stays confidential.

objection.text: Discover already publishes OpenAPI specifications for twelve partner products with no login, and Visa Acceptance's console already loads default sandbox credentials for signed-out readers. Neither a public reference nor a no-account console would be a first.

resolution.text: Both old headlines failed, and the card now makes the access point. The preview account is parity with Visa Developer and Mastercard, and decisions.md already settles it. The gain is one policy stated the same way on every surface.

cards.limit: Counts come from signed-out reads on 25 and 26 September 2026, and only Visa Token Service was opened among Visa's restricted products (visa-430). American Express's guide says some public sandboxes open automatically, while its catalogue flags none (amex-005). Send was never pressed on Visa Acceptance or Authorize.net, and Authorize.net sits outside the 25 networks. Mastercard's mapping document carries a Mastercard Confidential footer, and its product is absent from Mastercard's llms.txt (mastercard-425). The Partner Product Portal's page data switches on projects and API keys, so signed-in partners may already create keys there (dgn-204).

cards.title: Mastercard and American Express address rule changes by partner type, Visa by role at each member, and processors work out what applies

observed.text: Visa sends its weekly Business News to named roles at each member, and its risk guide makes clients responsible for obtaining risk communications on Visa Online.
A mirrored 2022 Mastercard announcement tags its audience by partner type, region and brand in a structured header.
American Express announces specification changes six months ahead each April and October, and Mastercard Send publishes a quarterly release schedule.
Issuer processors SoFi and Marqeta publish mandate logs for their clients, and SoFi says it reviews network mandates and updates its systems to match.
Acquiring platforms Braintree and Fiserv republish network changes for their merchants, each with an effective date.
UK acquirers told their regulator that Mastercard and Visa gave insufficient notice to avoid behavioural fees, and that scheme portals made information hard to reach.

inference.text: In the study's inference, a network can scope a notice to one partner only against configuration it holds, so configuration held at a processor still needs that processor's reading.
In the study's inference, scoping each notice to the partner takes on part of the triage that processors and acquiring platforms now publish for their clients.
In the study's inference, Discover sends processors fewer changes than Visa or Mastercard do, so a per-partner reading is a smaller job for it. The counts reflect only what each platform lists.

decision.question: Should each notice's Applies to line and the Notices page summary carry the partner's own scope, labelled as the network's reading with the rule text governing?
options: Scope each notice from configuration the network holds, label it as the network's reading, and say where configuration sits at the processor
Keep one notice per partner type, as Mastercard and American Express do, linked to the affected product pages
Filter each partner's notice list to only the changes that reach it
decision.evidence_favours: The first. Processors and acquiring platforms already publish per-client readings (mastercard-340, cross-255, mastercard-338), and UK acquirers reported short notice and hard-to-use scheme portals (cross-256, cross-257). The prototype's product pages already hold the scope. The study infers that filtering could hide a change that does apply. No source shows whether partners would rely on a network's reading.

position.text: Discover keeps product announcements behind EASI registration, as Visa and Mastercard gate their partner bulletins. American Express publishes merchant and specification change notices, and Visa publishes a merchant digest. American Express and Mastercard Send publish release schedules. The study found Discover's release cadence stated only in its 2024 10-K, though Marqeta dates an April 2026 Discover release.

means.text: The notice's Applies to line, the notice preview and the Notices page summary still say every acquirer on the network. Each should carry the product page's scope, such as Brightline Bank's BIN range for Disputes. The 2027 fee notice already gives the previous and new amounts. It should add the reason, as Australia's regulator expects.

The release message already tells the partner that nothing else in the release affects it. It should label that line as the network's reading, link the rule text as governing, and name any configuration held at the processor.

Put dated releases and a yearly count of changes that needed partner work beside the changelog, as American Express and Mastercard Send publish release schedules. The Brightline footer's Mandate calendar link can point there. A stated notice period waits on the timing ruling in i4.

Compliance already counts acknowledgements and decides waivers. It can show which partners each release reaches, and flag partners whose configuration sits at a processor, where the network's reading stops.

objection.text: Mastercard defines its Standards to include announcements and bulletins, so notice text can carry rule weight. A per-partner reading could become a second text that a partner cites if the reading proves wrong. The prototype already carries the notice fields, acknowledgement tracking and waivers.

resolution.text: The reading is labelled as the network's, with a link to the rule text, which governs. Scope comes only from configuration the network holds, and the notice says where configuration sits at the processor. Every notice stays listed, so a scoping error does not remove a change from view. Legal decides what standing the network's reading has.

cards.limit: Partner bulletins sit behind logins at Visa, Mastercard and Discover, and American Express runs its participant Knowledge Base behind a login (visa-166, mastercard-317, dgn-164, amex-079). The study therefore saw only public merchant and specification notices. Mastercard's header is known from one mirrored 2022 copy (mastercard-351). The study found no public network notice scoped to one partner, and gated portals may hold one.

cards.title: Severity-tiered support targets are rare, and this study found no public Discover incident record

observed.text: Seven of about ninety Mastercard product support pages publish response targets, and only Ethoca Alerts among them sets targets by severity.
Visa Acceptance promises developer support replies within one to two business days and sends production processing questions to Client Services.
Four Mastercard product support pages send service availability and outages to its API status page, and technical issues to a case with a one-business-day target.
Visa Acceptance runs a public status page with incident history, and Mastercard Developers shows per-service health and recent issues.
Discover's Command Center takes network connectivity issues around the clock, while its Operations Center for processors keeps weekday business hours.
This study found no public status page or incident record from Discover or PULSE, and Discover asks partners to report a data compromise within 48 hours.

inference.text: The UK regulator found issues with Visa's communications during Visa Europe's 2018 outage, and its crisis communications direction on Visa expired on 31 May 2024. The study infers that a network without a readable incident record risks the communication gap the regulator found at Visa.
The study infers that one severity-tiered promise across every product would be a difference, since no support page this study read offers one.

decision.question: When a live partner's authorisations fail, should the prototypes send it to the staffed operations line and a readable incident record, and keep case tiers for developer questions?
options: Keep the four-hour High case as the route for failing production authorisations, as the developer site does today
Send live failures to the staffed operations line and an incident record in the partner and developer views, and keep case tiers for developer and certification questions
Publish support targets product by product, as Mastercard does
decision.evidence_favours: The second. Visa Acceptance sends production processing questions to Client Services, and four Mastercard pages send outages to the status page (visa-372, mastercard-426). Visa Acceptance and Mastercard publish incident records, and this study found none from Discover (visa-376, mastercard-389, dgn-147). The line's stated hours follow the timing ruling in i4. The business sets staffing and commitments, and design makes the route and the record visible.

position.text: Discover's Command Center and 24-hour authorisation line match SHAZAM's round-the-clock client service. This study found no Discover response target or status page, while Visa Acceptance and Mastercard publish both.

means.text: Send failing production authorisations to the staffed network operations line and the status page, as Visa Acceptance and four Mastercard pages route live issues. The site files them today as a High case at four hours. Keep case tiers for developer and certification questions. The line's stated hours follow the timing ruling in i4.

The Partner Portal lists a 24-hour operations line and has no incident record. One resolved network operations note appears inside its latency report. Bring the developer site's incident record into the portal, and link the developer site's support page to that line.

The Agent Portal's clock gives a high case until the end of the day, while the Partner Portal promises four hours. Its inbox also sets resolution targets of two and five business days that no partner page shows. Once Rich rules on timings in i4, align the clock with the published promise and publish or drop the resolution targets.

PULSE's issuer page promises answered calls, and SHAZAM says it resolves more than 95% of service calls the same day. Present the staffed line and the incident record as parity with peers. Keep one severity-tiered promise across every product as the difference, pending the timing ruling.

objection.text: Ethoca already expects two to four hours for a production outage, and Visa Acceptance already runs one target across its developer products. Both peers publish status pages, so neither a promise nor an incident record is new.

resolution.text: The objection holds for the incident record and the staffed-line route, which close a Discover gap at parity. One severity-tiered promise across every product is the difference left, and it waits on the timing ruling in i4.

cards.limit: This study found no published member service levels, and a 2023 trade-body paper says Discover communicates host test results within agreed service levels (dgn-199). Visa Acceptance says contact methods vary by client agreement (visa-374). Discover's EASI offers partners a Message Center to its operations team behind a login, which may already carry incident notices (diners-043, dgn-386). A published target says nothing about how often it is met.

cards.title: Mastercard and Visa Acceptance run public status pages, none was found for Discover, and none of the four networks states a portal-wide version support period

observed.text: Mastercard's public status page shows each API's health in sandbox and production over the last 24 hours.
Visa Acceptance Solutions, which sells Cybersource and Authorize.net, runs a public status page with a sandbox group, incident history and email, SMS and feed alerts.
No public status page was found for the Visa Developer Center, American Express or Discover, whose Command Center takes network connectivity issues by phone around the clock.
None of the status pages found shows an availability percentage or a latency figure.
American Express publishes quarterly availability and response times for one open banking API, and EU rules require account providers to publish such statistics.
Visa's Installments notes support each version for up to three years with six months' notice, and none of the four networks states a portal-wide support period.

inference.text: The study infers a published availability or latency figure acts as a commitment, since the one network figure found is a disclosure EU rules require.
The study infers written incident communication carries regulatory weight. The UK Payment Systems Regulator directed Visa on crisis communications after Visa Europe's 2018 outage, until 31 May 2024.
The study infers a portal-wide support period is rare in form, since the version terms found cover single product families such as Visa Installments and Mastercard Processing.

decision.question: Which operational figures and promises should the developer site's status and versioning pages make in public?
options: States, 90 days of daily bars and a written incident record, adding a certification row and a feed, with no availability or latency figures
The same, plus the 99.99% availability figure, only once the business commits to publish it each quarter
Keep the prototype's 99.99% availability and 43 ms latency figures as they are
decision.evidence_favours: The first, moving to the second only on a business commitment. None of the status pages found shows such figures, and the one network figure found is a regulated disclosure (mastercard-w-status, visa-439, amex-454, cross-260). The 43 ms median is a timing, so Rich should rule whether the no-timings rule covers it. Whether a portal-wide support period can lead also waits on that ruling, though none of the four networks states one (visa-437, mastercard-021, amex-022, dgn-018).

position.text: No public status page or published deprecation policy was found for Discover, which offers a Command Center phone line. Mastercard and Visa Acceptance run public status pages with sandbox views.

means.text: A daily bar per product for 90 days gives a longer uptime record than Mastercard's 24 hours, while Cybersource keeps a longer incident history. The subtitle promises every environment, so add a certification row beside sandbox, and add a feed beside email as Visa Acceptance offers. Once Rich rules on timings in i4, state the support period in one wording, since the API reference and changelog differ. Add a security-fix exception, as Mastercard keeps.

Show the availability figure only if the business will publish and stand behind it, as American Express does for one open banking API. The 43 ms median issuer answer is a timing and needs Rich's ruling under the no-timings rule.

Name notice as the value, as panel 15, The Platform, with Insights, does in its Noticed on your traffic section. The ten-panel storyboard called this moment panel 9, Noticed Before She Had to Ask. Leave the status pages out of the story. The Partner Portal's 99.98% availability and 44 ms issuer answer follow the same timing ruling.

objection.text: Visa set a support period and notice for its Installments APIs, and Visa Acceptance runs a status page with a sandbox group. The prototype shows sandbox as one row with no certification row, so it trails Mastercard on environments.

resolution.text: The status page is parity, with a longer uptime record and fewer environments and alert channels. The portal-wide support period survives as rare in form, since the version terms found cover single product families. The story claim moves to notice, which panel 15 carries.

cards.limit: Gated client portals may carry status and notices inside, such as Mastercard Connect, the American Express Knowledge Base and SHAZAM's SystemChek, whose status address redirects to a login (mastercard-227, amex-371, shazam-011). Visa's Installments policy dates from 2020 and covers one API family (visa-437). American Express's Payment Gateway publishes a versioning policy with dated deactivations and no support period (amex-023). Interac's status page is known from a 2024 capture (interac-030).

cards.title: The US spend-management and Capital One business cards checked carry Visa or Mastercard, and the commercial programmes found on the network are in B2B travel

observed.text: Capital One's chief executive called the commercial card an important part of its future, and Capital One paid about 4.5 billion dollars for Brex.
More than five months after the 7 April close, Brex's site names Mastercard and Visa licences for its cards.
Capital One's business card page data tags each Spark and Venture Business card Visa or Mastercard, and Ramp, Mercury and Rho cards are issued under Visa or Mastercard licences.
Nium announced a Diners Club travel card in January 2025, and Pax2pay signed a Diners Club travel agreement in October 2024.
Discover's fintech page presents Mystifly, an air travel B2B payments firm, replacing cash and bank transfers with card payments through a solution built with the network.
Discover's DCX maps brands to parent companies, and its Restricted Access Network lets credit and prepaid issuers restrict purchases by business, category, brand or location.

inference.text: The study infers US commercial issuing on the network is small. The Fed found about 98% of roughly five million cards Discover classed commercial at end-2022 were consumer cards, leaving about 100,000 by the study's arithmetic. Discover's business card page has redirected to its consumer card list since March 2022.
The study infers supplier-locked virtual cards could reuse DCX brand mapping and the Restricted Access Network, though no source found shows either working on commercial ranges.
The study infers a near-term Brex move to the network is unlikely, since Capital One's chief executive put Brex's rapid growth ahead of a big integration.

decision.question: Which commercial-card story should the fintech and programme manager experience tell now?
options: Lead with Diners Club virtual cards for B2B travel, and show supplier-locked cards only as a labelled proposal
Tell a US spend-management story on the strength of the Brex purchase
Make no commercial claim until a named US commercial programme runs on the network
decision.evidence_favours: Diners Club B2B travel, with supplier-locked cards shown only as a labelled proposal. Nium announced a Diners Club travel card, and Mystifly pays by card through a solution built with the network (diners-059, dgn-388). Every US spend-management and Capital One business card checked carries Visa or Mastercard (dgn-280, cross-204, cross-205, cross-206, cross-201). US commercial ranges, any data rate and a DCX API stay with the business.

position.text: Discover is behind Visa, Mastercard and American Express in US commercial cards. Finexio, a US payables firm on Discover's fintech page, names Visa as its card network. The line-item data guides at Stripe, Adyen and Checkout.com do not name Discover. Visa sets purchasing and corporate Product 3, its line-item data rate, at 1.75% plus 10 cents against 2.70% plus 10 cents card not present. Visa, Mastercard and American Express each publish virtual card or supplier tools for developers, and Discover's seven public APIs include no DCX.

means.text: Lead the commercial offer for fintechs and programme managers with Diners Club virtual cards for B2B travel. Name Nium once its programme is confirmed live, and keep US commercial issuing a named ambition until a US programme runs on the network.

A new Products page can list Diners Club commercial cards and virtual card numbers with the countries where each runs. An allowed-suppliers control appears only as a labelled proposal, drawing on the Restricted Access Network, until it is confirmed on commercial ranges.

Publish a merchant lookup, drawn from DCX, that returns brand, parent company and locations for use in a spend rule. Name the line-item data fields the network reads, and what each earns, only once a Discover data rate is published.

Hold any US corporate card scene until Brex or another US programme runs on the network. A fintech variant set in B2B travel could show a Diners Club virtual card paying an airline, as Nium's airline payments offering describes.

objection.text: A counter-argument is that Capital One's chief executive put Brex's growth ahead of a big integration, so a network move can wait. Capital One is testing moving its own credit card accounts onto the network, so consumer credit may come first.

resolution.text: That argues for scoping the claim, and the recommendations do. The prototypes should make no US commercial claim until a named US programme runs on the network. The Diners Club travel offer rests on Nium's and Mystifly's programmes, which need no Brex decision. The owner calls the commercial card an important part of its future, so a fintech variant still needs a scoped answer for spend-management prospects.

cards.limit: Whether a US programme manager can get commercial ranges on Discover is not known. Whether DCX and the Restricted Access Network work on commercial ranges is not known. Discover's US interchange schedule is confidential, so any commercial or data rate is not public (dgn-064). The Spark networks come from page product data (dgn-280). Nium's and Pax2pay's announcements predate the Capital One close, and their live status was not rechecked (diners-059, diners-060). The study found no record of a plan to move Brex's cards onto the network (cross-201, dgn-279). American Express business cards were not in the check.

cards.title: Who absorbs the loss when an agent misreads an instruction is unsettled, and the study found no public Discover agent programme

observed.text: Mastercard says it enabled all US-based Mastercard cardholders for Agent Pay in 2025, and Visa's April 2026 rules set requirements for agentic payment enablers.
American Express says that in future it will protect eligible Card Members from charges related to a registered AI agent's error, with terms to apply.
Worldpay wrote in July 2026 that no liability shift exists yet and that frameworks have no clean answer for who absorbs a misread instruction.
Worldpay adds that American Express's cover protects the Card Member and leaves open what the merchant absorbs in a dispute over agent behaviour.
Stripe's agent tokens name Mastercard Agent Pay and Visa Intelligent Commerce, and Google's AP2 launch named Discover's alliance partners JCB and UnionPay International and did not name Discover.
None of the 59 pages that load from Discover Global Network's 61-entry sitemap mentions agentic commerce or AI agents.

inference.text: The study infers a network rule is still open to set. Worldpay says only the card networks can close the liability gap at scale.

The study infers Discover cards could reach agents through rivals' services without a Discover rule. Visa says its network-agnostic on-ramp lets agents pay with non-Visa cards, subject to availability.
The study infers low agent volume keeps the cost of setting a rule low now. American Express's innovation head said there had probably been as many press releases as transactions.

The study infers the owner has its own reason to act. Capital One's 10-K says agentic commerce may change when the merchant or issuer is liable. PULSE's June 2026 newsletter asked who is responsible when errors occur, and six banks including Capital One name liability management as an issue.

decision.question: Should Clearway and the developer site design for agent-initiated payments now, with a place for liability terms, while the business sets the misinstruction rule?
options: Design a labelled agent class, an issuer control and a place for liability terms now, and put a proposed dispute rule to the business
Wait for EMVCo's final framework and a business rule, and show nothing on agents
Claim agent readiness on the value proposition before any rule exists
decision.evidence_favours: The first. Worldpay, PULSE and six banks including Capital One all name agent liability as an open question (cross-221, pulse-087, cross-267). EMVCo's draft proposes agent indicators and shared intent records, so a labelled class rests on an emerging standard (cross-266, cross-265). The third would claim what none of Discover's public pages shows (dgn-390). Pricing the liability is the business's call.

position.text: Mastercard, Visa and American Express each run a named agent programme, and Stripe's tokens and Google's AP2 launch list do not name Discover. The study found no agentic commerce content on Discover's public site.

means.text: Put a rule to the business on who bears the loss when a registered agent misreads an instruction, for cards issued on Discover Network and for every acquirer. Base the evidence standard on a record of what the shopper asked the agent to do, which Worldpay calls the evidence that matters most.

List agent credentials beside stored tokens, with a sandbox and the liability terms readable without an account. Build on the draft framework from EMVCo, which Discover co-owns, as it settles. The draft proposes a shared layer for consumer-authorised intent, and Discover's stored tokens already limit use by channel and merchant.

Show agent-initiated payments as a labelled class in activity, disputes and reports, in line with the agentic transaction indicators EMVCo may add. Give issuers a control that limits what an agent may buy, as PULSE urges clear authorisation controls. No prototype mentions agent payments today.
Once a rule exists, show Marcus which partners have enabled agent-initiated payments. The agent portal has no such view today.

objection.text: A Discover executive could cite American Express's own remark that there have probably been as many press releases as agent transactions. A rule set before volume takes on liability that no source prices.

resolution.text: The rule can be a dispute right with an evidence standard, which the study infers limits payouts to claims that meet it. EMVCo's draft intent services could hold that evidence. Pricing the liability stays a business call the evidence cannot settle.

cards.limit: Absence rests on public pages and a sitemap scan, and Discover's gated portals were not seen (dgn-390). AP2's named list is partial (cross-223). EMVCo's framework is a draft open for comment until 30 September 2026, and the six banks call their principles a foundation for further discussion (cross-264, cross-268). The study found no public statement of Capital One's plans for agent payments on the Discover network (dgn-307).

cards.title: One sign-in and a shared onboarding record are both parity, and UnionPay's public guide describes one

observed.text: Visa and Mastercard link developer and client portal identities, and Mastercard pre-fills company data on its developer portal from Mastercard Connect.
UnionPay's Open Platform signs members in with their institution portal account and pre-fills each onboarding task with information UnionPay already holds.
UnionPay's May 2026 onboarding guide says its network engineers may edit a partner's connection details and return them for the partner to confirm.
The same guide links test reports into the partner's project, and UnionPay's project support manager confirms when integration testing is complete.
The Discover family uses separate entry routes for EASI, Advanced Payments, PULSE, fraud products and the Developer Center, though two Discover portals share one identity provider.
A 2023 U.S. Payments Forum paper says acquirers see Discover host simulator results at once and need not submit a test log, and Discover reviews each test.

inference.text: The study infers that Discover's host simulator already works as one testing record that the acquirer and Discover both read.

The study infers that one sign-in would carry little weight in a partner's choice to join. None of the study's 123 partner quotes concerns portal sign-in, though developers wrote 62 of them. Discover's 2024 annual filing, made before Capital One's purchase closed, names customisation of services and pricing as its grounds of competition.

The study infers that a shared record would also serve operations and fraud staff at acquirers and issuers after go-live. Gated tools such as FraudNet, OpsNet and Mastercom serve that work today, and the study found no partner source asking for a shared record.

decision.question: Should the prototypes treat one sign-in and a shared onboarding record as parity that closes a Discover gap, or sell the shared record as a reason to join?
options: Build both as parity, class the record as onboarding and operations value, and keep both out of the case for joining
Lead the story and marketing view with the shared record as Discover's difference
Hold the network-staff side of the record until partners are asked
decision.evidence_favours: The first. UnionPay's public guide describes a project record that its engineers and partners both change (unionpay-040, unionpay-042). Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay link partner identities (visa-031, mastercard-075, unionpay-016). None of the study's partner quotes concerns sign-in (mastercard-q17, visa-q11). Sign-in is process, so it stays out of the story under Rich's rule.

position.text: Discover's family asks partners through separate entry routes, while Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay link partner identities. UnionPay's public guide describes a shared project record. Discover's Partner Product Portal already switches on projects and a staged going-live flow to build on.

means.text: The story promises the network will not ask again, while Discover's family asks today through separate routes. The Company page already shows each fact on file and where it came from. Keep sign-in counts out of the story, since sign-in is process.

Build the partner project as one record that the partner, its developer and network staff all read and change, as UnionPay's guide describes. Pre-fill each task from facts on file, as UnionPay and Mastercard do. Let a partner administrator approve each person's access, as Mastercard Connect does. Where a rule asks again, as Mastercard Rule 7.10 asks sponsoring customers each year about their service providers, show the facts on file to confirm. Add interfaces tested and cases excluded to the certification record, as a 2023 trade-body paper says Discover's terminal letter lists them.

Marcus's single view has a public precedent in UnionPay's engineers and project support manager working on the partner's project. Let the network engineer propose a change to the partner's record and return it for the partner to confirm. Link test results into the same record, as UnionPay links its test reports.
Class one sign-in and the shared record as parity, and keep both out of the case for joining until partners say otherwise. Keep that case on the value of the network.

objection.text: One sign-in and a shared record give Discover no difference. Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay already link partner identities, and UnionPay's public guide already describes a project record its engineers and partners both change.

resolution.text: The objection holds, and the insight becomes a parity case. Discover's family asks through separate routes today, so building both closes a gap. Even Visa's single identity is partial, since its Digital Partner Services site lists four more sign-in portals.

cards.limit: The study read public pages only, so records behind Mastercard Connect, Visa Access or EASI stay unseen. UnionPay's guide describes the design and says nothing of how often engineers use it. Discover's Partner Product Portal links five partner tools (dgn-024), and how many an acquirer uses is not published. The Developer Center's Discover User ID sign-in redirects to didentity.okta.com, while two portals use identity.discoverglobalnetwork.com (dgn-392, dgn-196).

cards.title: Mastercard and Visa publish documentation for assistants, and Discover's Developer Center home and Partner Product Portal give a fetching tool a login page or a bare title

observed.text: Mastercard serves each documentation page as markdown, links llms.txt from its site footer and runs an MCP server that needs no sign-in.
Visa Acceptance publishes an llms.txt that links markdown pages and lists deprecated products that assistants should not recommend.
Visa documents an MCP server for its Developer Platform, whose Developer Center publishes no llms.txt.
The American Express developer portal and Discover's Developer Center, partner portal and network site publish no llms.txt.
Discover's Developer Center home is a noindex login page, and a plain fetch of its Partner Product Portal shows only the page title as text.
Visa's agent payment CLI drew 34,493 npm downloads in August 2026, against 1,513 for Mastercard's two documentation packages.

inference.text: The study infers the machine layer is catch-up work with little measured demand. Package downloads and GitHub stars are the only usage signals found, and none of the study's 123 partner quotes mentions assistants, llms.txt or MCP.

decision.question: When should the developer site add an llms.txt index and markdown twins of its public pages?
options: Now, as the next developer site change
After the access policy and status fixes, scoped to what the public table marks readable
Also build a documentation MCP server, as Mastercard and Visa run
Leave it out until partners ask for it
decision.evidence_favours: The second. Mastercard and Visa Acceptance already publish llms.txt, so this is parity work (mastercard-307, visa-440). Mastercard's two packages drew 1,513 npm downloads in August 2026, and none of the study's partner quotes asks for these tools (mastercard-411, mastercard-412). The evidence does not yet justify an MCP server.

position.text: Discover is behind Mastercard and Visa, which both publish documentation for assistants. It is level with American Express, whose portal also publishes no llms.txt.

means.text: The site has no llms.txt, markdown twin or MCP server today. Add an llms.txt index and a markdown twin of each public page after the access policy settles. List only what the site's public table marks readable without an account. Feed the changelog's deprecations into the index, as Visa Acceptance's file lists deprecated products.
Keep assistant-readable documentation off the value proposition, since it is parity with Mastercard and Visa. Agent payments are a separate question, taken up in the agentic liability card.

objection.text: Few developers use these tools, and Mastercard and Visa already have them, so adding them wins no lead.

resolution.text: The card survives as a sequencing decision. It closes a visible gap as parity work, after the access and status fixes.

cards.limit: Usage signals are package downloads and GitHub stars only, and remote MCP server use is not public (mastercard-411). One source records the footer linking a gated llms-full.txt, while the browser walk found llms.txt (mastercard-035, mastercard-w-dev). American Express's MCP position and the PIN networks' were not checked. The Developer Center's Explore APIs page does return readable text listing seven APIs (dgn-169). No source ties assistant-readable documentation to which network an acquirer or fintech joins.

decisions.question: Should every fee and interchange line a partner sees trace to its transaction, merchant, card class and rule, with included services listed beside it?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, and design can build it now. The Fed found Discover charged a commercial rate it did not disclose and had no classification controls (dgn-242, dgn-244). The consent order now requires those controls for each acquirer and merchant (dgn-245). Add interchange and card class per transaction to Brightline's cycle breakdown, and open Clearway's variance row to its transactions. Keep each flag and its correction in one record. State one promise that the four services Discover and PULSE call free come at no separate charge, and list them on each statement (dgn-294, dgn-295, pulse-032, pulse-075). Put a correction promise for every affected partner, and range data access terms, to the business and legal (cross-232, dgn-248). Keep the enforcement history out of the story.
decisions.would_change_it: Sight of the consent order's compliance plans, which go to the Reserve Bank and are not public, could show partner-facing controls already exist (cross-113, dgn-245). A US rule requiring fees acquirers can reconcile would turn the trace into parity, and the study found none. Discover pricing for tokens or account updating would widen or narrow the inclusion promise. Partner evidence that the promise does not weigh in network choice would move it off the value proposition. Confidence is high for the fee trace (i8). The inclusion promise rests on a medium-confidence card (included-services).

decisions.question: How should the acquirer, merchant and issuer experience present Discover Debit and PULSE now that the owner's debit cards carry exempt pricing?
decisions.recommendation: Scope every cost claim to the product where it holds, and rewrite the story's 'Lower cost on debit' as a measure on Brightline's own debit routes. Per transaction, Discover debit averaged more than exempt Visa and Mastercard debit in 2024 (dgn-077, cross-025, visa-462, mastercard-113). Show each acquirer the share and cost of its debit on the new Discover ranges, with declines named by cause (dgn-317, dgn-215). Split the issuer case by asset size, because the cap and net compensation rule bind covered banks on Discover as on Visa and Mastercard (cross-183, cross-185). Give acquirers a PULSE routing view on their own traffic, and the Side-by-Side token its own specification page (pulse-029, pulse-005). Publishing exempt rates, a token fee and incentive terms without cliffs are business calls.
decisions.would_change_it: Fed figures for 2025 could move the per-transaction comparison, since the table still showed 2024 as latest on 26 September 2026 (cross-228). Evidence that third-party exempt issuers receive the adviser-quoted rates would sharpen the issuer case (dgn-222). A public PULSE routed share or token usage figure would test the routing view (pulse-022, pulse-005). The Regulation II appeal could change the cap itself (cross-244). Confidence is high for the cost scoping (debit-cost-reversal). The asset-size split and routing parts rest on medium-confidence cards.

decisions.question: Should the story, value proposition and Clearway state reach as figures each partner can check, by partner type, dated and graded, including where payouts can land?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Acquirers see the inbound alliance brands and the BIN step (dgn-187, dgn-189). Issuers see the markets their cardholders gain, each with direction, release date and live grade (dgn-327, dgn-339). Grade each market for cards and ATMs with an as-of date, and lead US reach with Discover's 99% line and its Nilson source (dgn-252, dgn-346). Fix the story's alliance map, whose years fail against public releases for eleven of twelve alliances (dgn-325, dgn-336). Count push reach beside acceptance by showing issuers which originators pay out to their cards (cross-216, dgn-303). Give Discover Deliver a developer reference and sandbox (dgn-169). The business owns which alliances and originators go live.
decisions.would_change_it: Public alliance volume by direction, which the study did not find, could show which alliances deserve the lead. Published thresholds for the map's tiers would change how grades read (dgn-353). A public count of originators reaching Discover and PULSE cards would let push reach lead the value proposition as a figure (dgn-304). Confidence is high for alliances and market grades. The push part rests on a medium-confidence card.

decisions.question: Should deal and portal views show each partner its own economics as separate lines now, while the business decides whether to publish US schedules?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Show an acquirer its standard rate and any incentive on separate lines, since Discover competes on incentives and rebates whose amounts it does not disclose (dgn-071). Build margin views from merchant pricing the acquirer enters, since the acquirer sets the merchant's price (visa-249). Give ATM owners earnings per withdrawal, with interchange received and network fees as separate dated lines (cross-196, interac-013). Keep a blank incumbent-incentive line in the agent's deal flow. Discover's 28 million dollar deferred balance sits against capitalised balances in the billions at Visa and Mastercard, measured differently (dgn-382, visa-451, mastercard-415). Show totals over the contract term with no break-even date. A published US acquirer schedule and a PULSE ATM rate are business calls.
decisions.would_change_it: An acquirer or ATM owner source showing published rates move network choice would strengthen publication, and the study found none. Evidence that publication invites rate demands without volume would keep schedules private, since Capital One's deal case assumed existing pricing (dgn-221). Final approval of the Visa and Mastercard settlement would change what merchants can ask of cardholders (mastercard-413). Issuer tests of the incumbent-incentive line would settle whether partners ever see it.

decisions.question: Should the partner experience make the network's separation from its owner's issuing business checkable, by showing who reads each partner fact?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Show who can read each partner fact beside who supplied it, and give participants a log of network-side views. Neither merger approval's published text records a condition on how the networks treat other issuers or their data (cross-177, cross-178, cross-116). The fee assurance on record is a stated intent (cross-179, cross-250). Draft plain data-use and fair-treatment terms, marked as proposals for the business, since they may limit the owner's stated data plans (dgn-233). Keep service levels out under the no-timings rule.
decisions.would_change_it: A public report of a bank leaving PULSE or declining Discover over ownership would make written terms urgent, and the study found none. Sight of the commitments Capital One made to the Fed could show terms already exist (cross-251). Issuer interviews showing an access log does not answer the concern would move the weight to written terms.

decisions.question: Do the network's commitments on its own steps count as timings under 'No timings anywhere in the product', and what replaces the durations removed?
decisions.recommendation: Until Rich rules, every timing stays off every surface. For his ruling, the study proposes removing durations set by the partner's pace, internal estimates and journey ranges. It would keep a network commitment only where the business will stand behind it with an escalation route, as Mastercard does for Mastercom (mastercard-078, mastercard-418). Mastercard tells Send partners not to plan on its journey ranges (mastercard-081). It would show the owner of each step in place of the removed durations (mastercard-420). The same ruling settles the four-hour High case and the agent inbox's two and five business day targets (proto:developers/support.html, proto:story/brightline-story/src/js.txt). It also settles the developer site's 41 ms, 43 ms, 99.99% and 'within a second' (proto:developers/docs/index.html, proto:developers/status.html). It settles the Partner Portal's 44 ms and 99.98% too (proto:story/brightline-story/src/js.txt). It covers a booked certification window and the 24-month support period (proto:developers/changelog.html, proto:developers/api/index.html).
decisions.would_change_it: Partner interviews showing partners plan on hedged journey ranges would favour Visa's approach, since Visa says timing is nearly every client's first question (visa-427, visa-218). A business refusal to stand behind any commitment would move the ruling to removing every timing.

decisions.question: Should the network publish its dispute monitoring line and state that a dispute resolved early, including after a Fraud Alert, does not count against merchants or acquirers?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, as a proposal to the business, with the views designed now. Visa's monitoring and Mastercard's rules credit early resolution (visa-337, mastercard-215). The study found no public Discover line, and vendors cite about 1% and 100 chargebacks a month (dgn-288, dgn-376). Anchor early resolution on the free Fraud Alerts Standard tier (dgn-292). Add a prevented state beside open and charged-back cases in Clearway and on Brightline's Disputes page. Apply the same rules to Capital One cards and partner issuers' cards.
decisions.would_change_it: Sight of the gated Disputes Portal could show a line and tools already exist (dgn-122). Acquirer interviews showing a preference for case-by-case handling would favour publishing outcomes only. Confirmation that a refund after a Fraud Alert still counts as a dispute would weaken the anchor.

decisions.question: Should the acquirer's merchant view and the marketing pages argue merchant value from what network cardholders spend at each merchant, beside card counts?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Design owns the view, and the business owns releasing merchant-level sales data under the data-use terms proposed in d5. None of the pages in Discover's 61-entry public sitemap gives spend per card, ticket size or sales delivered (dgn-357). Capital One's chief executive said merchants ask how much volume a network brings (dgn-359). Add a per-merchant figure of sales from network cards to the acquirer's merchant view and the marketing sizer, with invented figures in the story. Date the 378 million card count and name its source (dgn-226). A network offers layer for partner issuers is a business decision (visa-090, amex-288).
decisions.would_change_it: Evidence that gated portals already give merchants such reporting would turn the work into surfacing it (dgn-231). Merchant interviews showing they cannot reconcile a network sales figure with their own statements would weaken it, and the study found no source either way. A business refusal to release merchant-level sales data would leave the view without figures.

decisions.question: Should the fintech and programme manager experience start inside the platforms that already carry Discover, and lead its commercial offer with Diners Club B2B travel?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Add a provider-first path and a public list of platforms carrying Discover by product and country. Stripe, Adyen, Highnote and Lithic document no Discover issuing, and Discover's fintech page names no provider (dgn-265, dgn-266, dgn-267, dgn-268, dgn-365). Marqeta states its platform is certified on Discover's April 2026 release (dgn-363). Lead commercial with Diners Club virtual cards for B2B travel (diners-045, dgn-388). Hold any US corporate card scene until a named US programme runs on the network (cross-201, dgn-279). Which platforms to court stays with the business.
decisions.would_change_it: Confirmation of Discover issuing at i2c, Fiserv, FIS or TSYS would lengthen the list, since these were not checked. A named US commercial programme on the network, such as Brex moving, would open a US spend-management story. Confirmation that DCX and the Restricted Access Network work on commercial ranges would lift the allowed-suppliers control out of proposal status. Confidence is high for the provider-first path. The commercial part rests on a medium-confidence card.

decisions.question: How should the network tell a live partner what changed and what broke, through scoped notices, a staffed operations route and a public incident record?
decisions.recommendation: Scope each notice's Applies to line from configuration the network holds, labelled as the network's reading with the rule text governing (mastercard-340, mastercard-179). Say where configuration sits at the processor (dgn-195). Send failing production authorisations to the staffed network operations line and a readable incident record (dgn-147, visa-372, mastercard-426). The line's stated hours follow the d6 ruling. Keep the status page to states, daily bars and written incidents, adding an availability figure only if the business commits to publish it (mastercard-w-status, amex-454). Add a certification row and a feed (mastercard-040, visa-188).
decisions.would_change_it: Sight of EASI's Message Center could show incident notices already reach partners (dgn-386). Legal advice on the standing of a network's reading would set how far scoping goes (mastercard-179). Partner interviews on whether they would rely on a scoped reading would settle it against a filtered list. Confidence is high for the operations route and status page. The notices part rests on a medium-confidence card.

decisions.question: Which single access policy and onboarding record should the developer site, Clearway and the story share?
decisions.recommendation: Adopt the preview account that decisions.md records, with a public reference and test cards and a sandbox key before a participation agreement. That matches Visa and Mastercard's self-serve sandboxes and is ahead of the invitation Discover requires today (visa-190, mastercard-002, dgn-034). Let the business scope what a preview key reaches, as Visa limits some actions to pre-approved clients (visa-432). Fix every surface that states another policy. Build one project record that the partner, its developer and network staff all read and change, as UnionPay's guide describes (unionpay-040). Keep sign-in and the record out of the case for joining. Add llms.txt and markdown twins after the access and status fixes (mastercard-307, visa-440).
decisions.would_change_it: Evidence that sign-in or a shared record weighs in the choice to join would move them into the value case. None of the study's 123 partner quotes concerns portal sign-in, though developers wrote 62 of them (mastercard-q17, visa-q11). Evidence that signed-in partners already create keys in the Partner Product Portal would narrow the gap (dgn-204). Measured developer demand for assistant-readable documentation would bring llms.txt forward (mastercard-411). Confidence is high for the access policy (i2). The shared record and assistant-readable parts rest on medium-confidence cards.

decisions.question: Should Clearway and the developer site design for agent-initiated payments now, with a place for liability terms, while the business sets the misinstruction rule?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Design a labelled agent class in activity, disputes and reports, an issuer control on what an agent may buy, and a readable place for liability terms. Build on EMVCo's draft agent indicators and intent services (cross-266, cross-265). Put a dispute rule for misread instructions to the business, with the shopper's instruction record as evidence (cross-263). Make no agent-readiness claim, since none of the 59 loading pages in Discover's sitemap mentions agentic commerce or AI agents (dgn-390).
decisions.would_change_it: EMVCo's final framework, after comment closes on 30 September 2026, could change the indicators (cross-264). A public statement of Capital One's agent plans on the network would set the scope (dgn-307). Measured agent volume would change how soon the rule matters (amex-130).

gaps.title: The US rate chart is confidential and card-class data needs an NDA, so partners cannot readily check the class behind a charge
gaps.why_major: From 2007 until at least 2023, Discover classed millions of consumer cards as commercial, its highest tier for acquirers and merchants (dgn-082, dgn-239). It did not disclose that it charged them the commercial rate (dgn-242). The Fed put the harm to acquirers and merchants near $1 billion (cross-114). Discover's US acquirer chart is confidential and opens only with an acquirer-issued code, and its fuller range table needs an NDA (dgn-063, dgn-064, dgn-248).
gaps.shore_up: Trace each fee and interchange line to its transaction, merchant, card class and rule, machine-readable at no cost. Keep each flag and its correction in one record. Show an acquirer its standard rate and any incentive on separate lines. Give developers a card range lookup, with access terms set by the business.

gaps.title: Merchants likely pay more on the owner's migrated debit cards, and those on flat-rate or tiered plans cannot see it
gaps.why_major: On a consultancy's quoted rate, a 50 dollar in-store sale costs 71 cents against 24.5 cents under the cap (dgn-212, dgn-214, dgn-078). On its figures merchants pay more unless their average in-store ticket is below 5.71 dollars (dgn-213). Stripe says the interchange would likely be higher (dgn-215). A merchant services firm says merchants cannot route these cards differently, and that flat-rate and tiered plans bury the new rate (dgn-314, dgn-315). Capital One lists a fall in large merchants accepting Discover or PULSE as a material risk (dgn-218).
gaps.shore_up: Drop family-wide lower-cost claims on debit, including the story's. Show each acquirer the share and cost of its debit on the new Discover ranges, with declines named by cause. Let Marcus see each acquirer's Discover debit share and cost, so he can raise the change first.

gaps.title: Capital One warns that some payroll providers may not support instant transfers to its new network debit cards
gaps.why_major: Capital One warns its own debit customers that Branch Messenger and PayActiv may not support instant transfers to the new cards (dgn-299, dgn-300). It attributes the change to the network the cards run on (dgn-301). Richmond Fed researchers say Visa Direct and Mastercard Send reach nearly all US debit cards (cross-218). The study found no Discover originator count and no public funds-transfer API (dgn-304, dgn-169).
gaps.shore_up: Show each issuer which originators pay out to its cards and which do not yet, starting with the providers Capital One names. Give Discover Deliver its own reference and sandbox. Track originator coverage as a network measure in the agent portal.

gaps.title: Discover's dispute line and how early resolution counts are not public
gaps.why_major: The study found no public Discover dispute rules or monitoring programme, and its Disputes Portal sits behind a login (dgn-122). Its line surfaces only through chargeback vendors, at about 1% and 100 chargebacks a month (dgn-288, dgn-376). Visa's monitoring and Mastercard's rules credit disputes resolved early (visa-337, mastercard-215). A vendor says Ethoca and CDRN coverage of Discover is thin (dgn-377).
gaps.shore_up: Publish the line, the evidence standard, any fee and how early resolution counts. Add a prevented state beside open and charged-back cases in Clearway and on Brightline's Disputes page. Show Marcus which acquirers and payment facilitators are nearing the line before any consequence applies.

gaps.title: PULSE's public pages state no ATM rate, and Discover's map shows no ATM coverage in most Caribbean island markets
gaps.why_major: NCR Atleos says networks set what deployers are paid (cross-196). PULSE's ATM pages claim competitive interchange and state no amount, while Visa, Mastercard and Interac publish ATM interchange (pulse-085, visa-467, mastercard-094, interac-013). Discover's map shows no ATM coverage in 24 of 27 Caribbean island markets (dgn-352). Capital One names the Caribbean among its customers' top four destinations and points debit holders to Discover and PULSE ATMs (dgn-259, pulse-067).
gaps.shore_up: Lead the ATM owner view with earnings per withdrawal, with interchange and network fees as separate dated lines. Carry the 15 high-acceptance markets with no ATM bank as a recruitment list in Sonia's seat. Return the surcharge-free flag from the ATM Locator API.

gaps.title: Discover's public pages do not show fintechs where Discover is carried
gaps.why_major: Stripe, Adyen, Highnote and Lithic document Visa and Mastercard issuing and no Discover issuing (dgn-265, dgn-266, dgn-267, dgn-268). Discover's fintech page names no processor, sponsor bank or programme manager (dgn-365). Its Partner Directory holds only tap-on-mobile and stored-token products (dgn-366). The US spend-management and Capital One business cards checked carry Visa or Mastercard (dgn-280, cross-204, cross-205, cross-206).
gaps.shore_up: Publish a list of platforms carrying Discover by country and product. Add a provider-first story path that begins inside Marqeta or SoFi Tech Solutions. Let Clearway records inherit facts from the processor with the source named. Lead commercial with Diners Club B2B travel.

gaps.title: Partner issuers compete with the network's owner, and no published approval condition covers their treatment or data
gaps.why_major: Capital One's banking businesses compete with banks and credit unions for loans and deposits (pulse-076). Neither the Fed order nor the OCC letter records a condition on how the networks treat other issuers or their data (cross-177, cross-178, cross-116). The Fed approval also rests on commitments the study could not see (cross-251). Capital One valued these partner relationships at 1.5 billion dollars, partly on estimated attrition (pulse-060, pulse-081). The study found no public report of a departure.
gaps.shore_up: Show who can read each partner fact beside who supplied it, with a partner-visible log of network-side views. Draft plain data-use and fair-treatment terms, marked as proposals for the business.

gaps.title: Analysts say a large issuer that switches puts incumbent incentives at risk
gaps.why_major: Visa and Mastercard carried 7.3 and 10.4 billion dollars of capitalised incentives in 2025 (visa-451, mastercard-415). Discover's deferred incentive balance was 28 million dollars at end-2024 (dgn-382). The accounting differs, so the comparison is indicative. Capital One warns it may be unable to offer Network Partners adequate pricing while keeping sufficient net revenue (dgn-293). Two analyst sources, speaking about a possible sale of Fiserv's debit networks, name lost incentives as a cost of a big bank's switch (visa-453, cross-253).
gaps.shore_up: Keep a blank incumbent-incentive line in the agent's deal flow so partner managers price against the issuer's alternative. Show partners net economics over the contract term with no break-even date. Pricing stays the business's lever.

gaps.title: Discover's public pages give merchants facing higher debit interchange card counts and no sales figure
gaps.why_major: None of the pages in Discover's 61-entry public sitemap gives spend per card, ticket size or sales delivered (dgn-357). Stripe told cost-plus merchants that migrated Capital One debit would likely carry higher interchange (dgn-215). Capital One's chief executive said merchants ask how much volume a network brings (dgn-359). American Express argues from spend per card (amex-448).
gaps.shore_up: Add a per-merchant figure of sales from network cards to the acquirer's merchant view and the marketing sizer. Date each figure and name its source. The business decides what merchant-level data it releases.

gaps.title: The study found no public status page or incident record from Discover
gaps.why_major: The study found no public status page or incident record from Discover or PULSE (dgn-147, pulse-037). Visa Acceptance and Mastercard publish both (visa-376, mastercard-040). Discover's Operations Center for processors keeps weekday business hours (dgn-146). UK acquirers reported insufficient notice and hard-to-reach portal information at Visa and Mastercard (cross-256, cross-257). EASI's gated Message Center may already carry incident notices (dgn-386).
gaps.shore_up: Send failing production authorisations to the staffed network operations line and a readable incident record, and bring that record into the Partner Portal. The line's stated hours follow the d6 ruling. Scope each notice to the partner's configuration, labelled as the network's reading.

gaps.title: Developers cannot reach a Developer Center sandbox until a representative invites them
gaps.why_major: Discover's Developer Center admits developers only by a representative's invitation (dgn-034). Visa and Mastercard open a sandbox for most APIs to any registered developer before a commercial agreement (visa-190, mastercard-002). The Discover family asks partners through separate entry routes (dgn-174, pulse-039, dgn-002).
gaps.shore_up: Adopt the preview account policy on every surface. Build one shared project record the partner, its developer and network staff all read and change. Treat both as parity.

gaps.title: The study found no public Discover agent programme or liability rule
gaps.why_major: Mastercard, Visa and American Express each run a named agent programme (mastercard-364, visa-409, amex-126). Stripe's agent tokens and Google's AP2 launch list do not name Discover (cross-222, cross-223). Worldpay says what a merchant absorbs in a dispute over agent behaviour is open (cross-261). American Express's innovation head said there had probably been as many press releases as agent transactions (amex-130).
gaps.shore_up: Design a labelled agent class, an issuer control on what an agent may buy, and a readable place for liability terms. Put a misinstruction dispute rule to the business.

advantages.title: Fee lines a partner can trace to card class and rule
advantages.why_credible: The consent order already requires Discover to build controls that classify cards and assess interchange for each acquirer and merchant (dgn-245). Large UK acquirers said they must buy extra services or consultancy from the schemes to understand their fees (cross-191). Visa and Mastercard each told the UK regulator they could not give fee logic for all fees within a year (cross-229). The PSR deferred that duty only for fees earning £850,000 or less a year, a small share of fee revenue (cross-230). Acquirers can request that data meanwhile (cross-230). The UK direction covers scheme and processing fees and leaves out interchange (cross-065). This map infers that a free trace of each line to card class and rule would go beyond what the UK requires of Visa and Mastercard.
advantages.press: Lead the acquirer value claim with a statement its finance team can reconcile, each line tied to transaction, card class and rule. Once Discover confirms its controls, say who sets each card's class. Keep the enforcement history out of the story.

advantages.title: The owner's own cardholders as a reason for merchants to accept
advantages.why_credible: Trade press reports Capital One has moved about 25 million debit cards onto Discover (dgn-216). A merchant services firm says refusing them means losing the sale (dgn-316). Capital One is testing moving its own credit accounts onto the network (dgn-249, cross-117). This map infers that Visa and Mastercard cannot match this, since neither issues cards (visa-466, mastercard-153). American Express issues its own cards and argues from their spend, so this map infers the edge does not hold against it (amex-204, amex-448).
advantages.press: Name the owner's cardholders on the network as a reason for Brightline's merchants to accept, with no cost claim. Pair it with the who-reads-each-fact view, since the same ownership opens the separation gap. Show sales from those cards per merchant once live.

advantages.title: Services that come with the network, on a lighter change load
advantages.why_credible: Discover and PULSE publicly call four services free or no cost (dgn-294, dgn-295, pulse-032, pulse-075). In April 2026 Visa and Mastercard each added services to a US bundle fee and raised its rate (visa-465, mastercard-421). Visa's value-added services revenue grew 24% against 11% for net revenue (visa-071, visa-464). This map infers matching the promise would cost an incumbent part of a fast-growing line. Fiserv's spring 2026 notice listed four Discover items against 16 Visa and 12 Mastercard (cross-248). The counts reflect only what each platform lists (dgn-296, cross-248, cross-249). American Express also calls its Enhanced Authorization free, so the contrast is with Visa and Mastercard (amex-453).
advantages.press: State one promise across Discover and PULSE naming each included service beside the partner type it serves. List included services at no charge on each statement. Publish a yearly count of changes that needed partner work beside the changelog.

advantages.title: Alliances with domestic networks since 2005, six stated in their releases as two-way
advantages.why_credible: Public releases date alliances from UnionPay in 2005 to Uzcard in January 2026 (dgn-325, diners-049). The 2005 release describes UnionPay cards accepted on PULSE (dgn-325). Releases say RuPay, Verve, Troy, NAPAS, mada and Uzcard run both ways (dgn-327, dgn-328, dgn-330, dgn-331, dgn-333, diners-058). This map infers that agreements negotiated one by one over two decades are slow to replicate. The study found no source ranking alliance breadth, and Visa and American Express hold some such links (amex-235, visa-064). The study infers that announcements alone overstate live reach, since Discover's map shows no acceptance in Uzbekistan and Nigeria (dgn-339, dgn-340).
advantages.press: Show issuers the markets their cardholders gain and acquirers the brands their merchants can take, each with direction, release date and live grade. Cite growth with Discover's fastest-growing line and its footnote (dgn-338).

advantages.title: A routable card-on-file debit token, an edge over Visa and Interlink only
advantages.why_credible: PULSE says its Side-by-Side Token Service routes tokenised card-on-file debit over PULSE and other enabled unaffiliated networks (pulse-029). DOJ's complaint alleges tokenised card-not-present debit may be effectively non-contestable (visa-463). Visa and Interlink now charge merchants per card-not-present token authorisation (visa-414, interlink-001). Against NYCE, STAR and Accel it is parity, since each lists tokenised debit (nyce-013, star-010, accel-009). PULSE publishes no fee for its own token service, so the fee contrast waits on that figure (pulse-005). The DOJ claims are allegations, with motions due in August 2027 (cross-049).
advantages.press: Give the token its own developer page with a readable specification and fee, where PULSE today offers a contact form. Show in Clearway which networks each token can route to. Make no claim that PULSE heads a least-cost table.

advantages.title: Early dispute resolution anchored on a free alert tier
advantages.why_credible: Discover's Fraud Alerts Standard tier is free, and Discover markets Fraud Alerts to help prevent chargebacks (dgn-292, dgn-375). A dispute-analytics vendor says merchants pay for chargeback alerts per alert, whatever the outcome (cross-210). This map infers an alert provider matching a free tier would give up per-alert fees. Whether a refund after an alert keeps a dispute out of any count is unknown.
advantages.press: Once the business sets the rule, publish that a dispute resolved before chargeback does not count against the merchant or acquirer. Build early resolution on the free tier with no per-alert fee.

advantages.title: A graded, dated market map already in public
advantages.why_credible: Discover's map grades card and ATM acceptance market by market, and the partner Reach page links to it (dgn-252, dgn-355). In the sources checked, American Express and Mastercard state reach as totals (amex-217, mastercard-144). No card shows a barrier to a rival publishing grades, so the lead is checkability alone. Grades invite comparison of 110 markets with Visa's more than 200 and Mastercard's more than 210 (visa-044, mastercard-143).
advantages.press: Grade each market for cards and ATMs with an as-of date. Lead US reach with Discover's 99% line and its Nilson source (dgn-346). In Clearway, show issuers their cardholders' destinations against the grades.

open_questions.question: Would a published US acquirer schedule win acquirer volume, or only invite rate demands?
open_questions.why_unknown: No source shows publication would win volume, and Capital One's deal case assumed existing network pricing (dgn-221). Discover's US rates, incentives and acquirer margins are not public (dgn-064, dgn-071).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Interview acquirers on how they present Discover to merchants today. Put the pricing question to the network's business team with those findings.

open_questions.question: Do third-party exempt issuers receive the Discover Debit rates advisers quote for Capital One's migrated cards?
open_questions.why_unknown: The rates found are adviser quotes, and whether other issuers receive them is not public (dgn-222, dgn-212). The Fed's 2024 Discover average mostly reflects Discover's own cards (cross-109).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask the network's pricing team. Interview community banks, credit unions and programme managers on Discover Debit yield.

open_questions.question: Which originators push to Discover and PULSE cards today, and which do not?
open_questions.why_unknown: The study found no public originator count (dgn-304). Current eligibility at Branch, PayActiv and PayPal was not checked.
open_questions.how_to_settle: Pull originator enablement data from the business. Test payouts to a Discover debit card at the providers Capital One names.

open_questions.question: Which announced alliances are live, in which direction, and what volume does each carry?
open_questions.why_unknown: Release dates mark announcements, and live acceptance can follow later. The study found no public alliance volume, and Capital One reports one Global Payment Network figure (dgn-344).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask the network team for each alliance's status and volume by direction, and check each against the map's grades.

open_questions.question: What do the map's H, G and J tiers measure, and why does 185 sit beside 110 graded markets?
open_questions.why_unknown: The map code labels the tiers and publishes no thresholds (dgn-353). No page read explains the gap between 185 and 110.
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask the map's owners for tier thresholds and the scope of each count before any grade enters a prototype.

open_questions.question: Are the consent order's classification controls in place, and can the network say who sets each card's class?
open_questions.why_unknown: The compliance plans go to the Reserve Bank and are not public (cross-113, dgn-245).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask the business and legal before statement copy names who sets each card's class.

open_questions.question: Do partner issuers see the owner as a threat to their data or treatment, and would an access log answer it?
open_questions.why_unknown: The study found no public report of a bank leaving PULSE over ownership. The Fed approval also rests on commitments the study could not see in full (cross-251).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Interview community bank and credit union issuers on Discover Debit and PULSE with the access-log prototype. Ask the business what commitments exist.

open_questions.question: What is Discover's dispute monitoring line, and does a refund after a Fraud Alert keep a dispute out of the count?
