open_questions.why_unknown: Discover's dispute rules are not public, and its line surfaces only through vendors (dgn-122, dgn-288). The gated Disputes Portal may hold it.
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask the network's disputes team. Interview acquirers on whether they prefer a published line or case-by-case handling.

open_questions.question: What do the gated partner portals already offer?
open_questions.why_unknown: The study read public pages only. EASI, the Disputes Portal and the signed-in Partner Product Portal may hold notices, incident messages, merchant reporting and API keys (dgn-164, dgn-386, dgn-231, dgn-204).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Walk the gated portals with the network team before Clearway duplicates anything they hold.

open_questions.question: Which network commitments would partners plan around, and would they rely on a network's per-partner reading of a notice?
open_questions.why_unknown: Visa says timing is nearly every client's first question, while Mastercard tells Send partners not to plan on its ranges (visa-427, mastercard-081). Mastercard defines announcements as part of its Standards (mastercard-179). No source measures partner reliance.
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask acquirers, issuers and processors in interviews which commitments and readings they would act on. Feed the answers to the i4 ruling and to legal.

open_questions.question: If Rich's d6 ruling admits network commitments, would one portal-wide support period and one severity-tiered support promise set Discover apart?
open_questions.why_unknown: Both are timings, and the ruling is open (i4). None of the four networks states a portal-wide support period (visa-437, mastercard-021, amex-022, dgn-018). Among Mastercard's product support pages, only Ethoca Alerts sets targets by severity (mastercard-402, mastercard-401).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Rich rules on d6, then the business says whether it will stand behind each commitment.

open_questions.question: How would a large issuer read a deal view that shows the incumbent incentives it puts at risk?
open_questions.why_unknown: The study has no source on how issuers would read such a view. Individual deal and clawback terms are not public (mastercard-105).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Test the agent deal flow with partner managers, then with a small set of issuer prospects.

open_questions.question: What does PULSE pay an ATM deployer per withdrawal, and do the reissued debit cards carry another ATM network?
open_questions.why_unknown: Neither is public. PULSE Select's product page now redirects, so whether it still enrols institutions is unclear (pulse-082).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask PULSE for its current ATM schedule and Capital One for the reissued cards' ATM marks. Interview ATM deployers on what they need before joining.

open_questions.question: Can a US programme manager get commercial ranges on Discover, and do DCX and the Restricted Access Network work on them?
open_questions.why_unknown: No source found answers either question, and Discover's US interchange schedule is confidential (dgn-063, dgn-064).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Ask the business, then confirm with a processor that carries Discover, such as Marqeta or SoFi Tech Solutions.

open_questions.question: Who should bear the loss when a registered agent misreads an instruction on a card issued on Discover Network, and at what cost?
open_questions.why_unknown: Worldpay says no liability shift exists yet, and no source prices the liability (cross-220, amex-130). EMVCo's framework is a draft open for comment until 30 September 2026 (cross-264).
open_questions.how_to_settle: Put a proposed dispute rule to the business and legal, and revisit it once EMVCo publishes its final framework.

map.order_basis: Ranked by card confidence, high before medium. Within each level, a card whose gap is a charge US partners bear comes first, current before past. Next comes i4, since i2, i6 and i10 wait on its timing ruling. The rest keep the earlier map's order.

tested.title: One login is the gap the market leaves open
tested.change: Merged with i9 and i12. One sign-in is parity with Visa and Mastercard, and UnionPay's public guide already describes a shared onboarding record.

tested.title: Reading without an account is the market floor, and Discover sits below it
tested.change: Merged with i3. Reading is mostly open at the large networks, and each developer centre still asks for an account before a sandbox key.

tested.title: Nobody lets a stranger send a request
tested.change: Visa's acceptance consoles ship with default sandbox credentials, so the first version's claim fell.

tested.title: The contract gate is universal, so show it as a step
tested.change: Merged with i5 and part of i12. Showing the gate as a timed step would break the rule of no timings in the product.

tested.title: A published turnaround is rare, and it is always the network's own
tested.change: Turnarounds are published more often than claimed, and not only for the network's own steps. Its recommendation conflicted with the rule of no timings.

tested.title: Status and change pages put the prototype at the top of the field
tested.change: Status pages are parity. Visa's acceptance platform runs one too, and no network states a portal-wide version support period.

tested.title: Rule changes reach partners by bulletin, in a separate place
tested.change: Mastercard and American Express already address changes by partner type, so the gap is narrower than first stated.

tested.title: Fee transparency is arriving by regulation
tested.change: Reframed around fee lines that trace to each transaction, after the Federal Reserve's finding on misclassified cards.

tested.title: The documentation now has two readers
tested.change: Machine-readable documentation is a catch-up step for Discover, whose pages give a fetching tool a login page or a bare title.

tested.title: Support promises are almost absent, so the four-hour line stands out
tested.change: Narrowed to what public support pages show. Severity tiers are rare, and no public Discover incident record was found.

tested.title: Alliances are Discover's product no other network sells
tested.change: Alliances run in both directions, and most dates on the story's alliance map have no public source.

tested.title: Certification detail is where the prototype exceeds every network
tested.change: Split between insights 23 and 5. The first version's claim that no network shows certification detail was mostly false.
